title: Galli 2015 wheelchair full-body PPS
citation: Galli, G., Noel, J. P., Canzoneri, E., Blanke, O., & Serino, A. (2015). The wheelchair as a full-body tool extending the peripersonal space. Frontiers in Psychology, 6, 639.
notes: Wheelchair-training PPS task. The profile captures the reported front/back trunk PPS timing and trial formula; the original 16-speaker Gaussian-amplitude arrays are represented as two virtual moving-source trajectories while active/passive/blindfolded wheelchair training remains experiment context.

reference_parameters.reported_trial_formula: 216 PPS-assessment trials: 12 front/back spatial locations x 12 repetitions = 144 audio-tactile trials, plus 24 auditory catch trials and 48 tactile-only baseline trials.
reference_parameters.apparatus_recreation_policy: The two physical 8-speaker Gaussian-amplitude arrays are treated as apparatus provenance and represented by the toolkit's front and back binaural moving-source trajectories using the reported 2 m path and 75 cm/s speed.
remaining_caveats: exact original per-speaker Gaussian gain synthesis
wheelchair training condition is represented as experiment context rather than a generated WAV factor

tactile_sites: front/back trunk site (sternum/back mapped by trajectory side)

provenance.source: Frontiers methods report tactile delays at 380, 760, 1140, 1520, 1900, and 2280 ms from sound onset.
Methods report 144 audio-tactile trials, 24 auditory catch trials, and 48 tactile baseline trials.
